title: Applying Interrogation Resistance Training Research to Model Probe Hardening
original_idea: Survey interrogation resistance tactics. Identify analogous capabilities a scheming model would need. Test whether these correlate with scheming sophistication. Design probe strategies to counter each resistance mechanism.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: understand probe resistance -> design counter-probe strategies -> stay ahead in detection arms race. Names a real dynamic but the gap is whether interrogation resistance psychology transfers meaningfully to LLM behavioral probing. The analogy may be too loose.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The survey component and probe design are accessible. Testing correlation with scheming sophistication requires access to models with varying scheming capability, which is harder. The cross-domain literature review is manageable for CS students with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple workstreams: literature survey, capability mapping, correlation testing, probe design. Each is a substantial task. No obvious bounded first experiment that stands alone -- the survey alone is not a safety contribution without the testing component.

novelty.reasoning: The cross-disciplinary analogy between human interrogation resistance and AI model probe resistance is creative and largely unstudied. While deception detection in AI models is well-researched (linear probes, activation patching, behavioral probing), and human interrogation psychology is its own field, the explicit mapping of interrogation resistance tactics to model probe evasion strategies has not been directly attempted. Sarkadi's 'Deception Analysis with Artificial Intelligence: An Interdisciplinary Perspective' (arXiv:2406.05724) is the closest work, surveying deception from an interdisciplinary lens but not specifically mapping interrogation resistance mechanisms to AI probe hardening. The observation that 'training out scheming may teach more covert scheming' (OpenAI, 2025) is tangentially related but does not use the interrogation framework. The analogy may be loose, but the specific research program of systematically cataloging resistance mechanisms and designing counter-probes is novel.
